Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness﴾. He mentioned another proof of His power in the human being himself, so that he may take heed. The meaning of "from weakness" is from a weak drop (nutfah). It is also said: "from weakness" means in a state of weakness, which is what they were at the beginning, in childhood and infancy.

(Then He made after weakness strength) meaning youth (al-shabibah).

(Then He made after strength weakness) meaning old age (al-haram). ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah recited it with a fatḥah on the ḍād in all three instances, while the rest recited it with a ḍammah. Both are dialectal forms, and the ḍammah is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Jaḥdarī recited "min ḍaʿfin thumma jaʿala min baʿdi ḍaʿfin" with a fatḥah in both places and "ḍuʿfan" with a ḍammah only, intending to combine the two dialects. Al-Farrā' said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh, and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamim. Al-Jawharī said: al-ḍaʿf and al-ḍuʿf are the opposite of strength. It is also said that al-ḍaʿf with a fatḥah is used of opinion, and with a ḍammah of the body, and from this is the ḥadīth about the man who was deceived in transactions: (that he buys while there is weakness in his ʿuqdah [i.e., in his judgment and consideration of his own interests]). "Shaybah" is a verbal noun like "shayb," and a verbal noun may stand for the whole clause; the same applies to "ḍaʿf" and "quwwah."

(He creates what He wills) meaning of strength and weakness.

(And He is the All-Knowing) in His management.

(The All-Powerful) over His will. The Kufan grammarians permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with a fatḥah on the ʿayn, and likewise every case in which a guttural letter occurs as the second or third radical.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾, meaning: the polytheists will swear oaths.

(They will say: "We remained not but an hour.") There is nothing in this that contradicts the punishment of the grave (ʿadhab al-qabr), since it has been authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ through more than one chain that he sought refuge from it and commanded that refuge be sought from it. Among that is what ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud reported, who said: The Prophet ﷺ heard Umm Habibah saying: "O Allah, let me enjoy my husband, the Messenger of Allah, and my father Abu Sufyan, and my brother Muʿawiyah." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "You have asked Allah for appointed terms and apportioned provisions, but rather ask Him to protect you from the punishment of Hell and the punishment of the grave." This is in well-known hadiths narrated by Muslim, al-Bukhari and others. We have mentioned a portion of them in the book (al-Tadhkirah).

Regarding the meaning of "They remained not but an hour," there are two views. The first: there will be a pause (khamdah) before the Day of Resurrection, and on this view they say: "We remained not but an hour." [The part between the brackets is missing from manuscript Sh.] [The other view: they mean in the worldly life, because it passed and ended, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46], as if they had not remained but an hour of a day, even though they swore about the unseen and about what they did not know. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: [The part between the brackets is missing from manuscript Sh.]] And ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾, meaning: they used to lie in the worldly life. It is said: "The man was turned away (ufika)" when he was diverted from truthfulness and goodness. And "a land ma'fuka" means one withheld from rain. A group of people of speculative theology claimed that in the Hereafter there cannot be any lying, given their state, but the Qur'an indicates otherwise. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "Thus they were turned away," meaning: just as they were diverted from the truth in their oath that they remained not but an hour, so they used to be diverted from the truth in the world. And He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿On the Day Allah raises them all up, they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 18]. And He said: ﴿Then their trial was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Look how they lied﴾ [al-An'am: 23–24].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained according to the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection."﴾ There is difference of opinion concerning "those who were given knowledge." It is said they are the angels. It is said they are the prophets. It is said they are the scholars of the (previous) nations. It is said they are the believers of this Ummah. It is said they are all the believers, meaning that the believers will say to the disbelievers, in reply to them, "You have indeed remained in your graves until the Day of Resurrection."

The fa' in His saying, "So this is the Day of Resurrection," is a response to an implied condition indicated by the context. Its meaning is: "If you were denying the Resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection." Ya'qub related from some reciters, and it is the reading of al-Hasan, "ila yawmi al-ba'th" (إِلى يَوْمِ الْبَعْثِ) with a vowel (tahrik) on the letter, and this is one of the cases in which there is a throat letter (harf min huruf al-halq) (i.e., a letter pronounced from the throat, which affects the vowel of the preceding letter).

It is also said: the meaning of "according to the Book of Allah" is "according to the judgment of Allah." It is also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the sentence, meaning: "And those who were given knowledge in the Book of Allah and the faith said, 'You have indeed remained until the Day of Resurrection.'" This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Al-Qushayri said: according to this view, "those who were given knowledge" means the Book of Allah.

It is also said: they are those for whom the Book has ruled that they have knowledge. "So this is the Day of Resurrection," that is, the day you used to deny.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 30, verse 57:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾, meaning: knowledge of the Resurrection will not benefit them, nor will apologizing on that Day. It was also said: when the believers refuted them, they asked to be returned to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted as excused.

(And they will not be asked to make amends) meaning: nor will their condition be that of one who is asked to make amends and return. It is said: "I asked him to make amends (istaʿtabtuhu), and he granted me amends (aʿtabani)," meaning: I sought his pleasure and he pleased me, and this is when I have wronged him. The literal meaning of aʿtabtuhu is: I removed his grievance (ʿatb). Its explanation will come in "Fussilat" [[See vol. 15, p. 351 onward.]]. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾi read "fa-yawma'idhin lā yanfaʿu" with the yāʾ (ya), while the rest read it with the tāʾ (ta).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, meaning: every kind of example that guides them to what they need, and alerts them to the Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the truthfulness of the Messengers.

(﴿And if you bring them a sign﴾), meaning a miracle, such as the splitting of the sea and the staff, and others (﴿the disbelievers will surely say: "You are not but falsifiers"﴾), O assembly of believers.

(﴿You are not but falsifiers﴾), meaning: you follow falsehood and magic. (﴿Thus﴾), meaning: just as Allah sealed their hearts so that they do not understand the signs from Allah, so likewise ﴿Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know﴾ the proofs of Tawhid. (﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾), meaning: be patient with their harm, for Allah will support you. (﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you light [in faith]﴾), meaning: let them not provoke you away from your religion. It was said: he is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and what is intended is his community. It is said: "istakhaffa fulan fulanan," meaning he made him foolish until he led him to follow him in error. It is in a jussive position due to the prohibition, emphasized with the heavy nun, and so it is built on the fatha, just as two things are built when one is joined to the other. "Those who do not have certainty" is in a nominative position. Some Arabs say "al-ladhuna" in the nominative position. This has already been discussed in "al-Fatiha" [[see vol. 1, p. 148.]].
